Fix the System.name: Fix the System
Fix the System.description:
🏛️ Hero society is broken somewhere: rankings, laws, prejudice or the people at the top. You mean to change it, from inside or out.

🧭 This motivation shapes the chances the story offers: student government, journalism, insiders, legal cases and protests.
⚠️ The system pushes back, small wins cost allies, and extremists offer violent shortcuts.
⚖️ Every side gets a fair hearing, and your methods are always your choice.
Fix the System.traitNarrativeEffects: The character sees a flaw in hero society and wants it changed: rankings that reward publicity, laws that criminalize ordinary Quirk use, prejudice against heteromorphs and the Quirkless, how villains are made and punished, or what the Hero Public Safety Commission keeps hidden. The narrator surfaces ways to push: student government, journalism, hero work with a public voice, insiders at agencies and the Commission, legal cases, protests and leaks. It brings in reformers, cynics, officials who defend the system, and extremists on both sides of the law who offer violent shortcuts. Pressures: the system pushes back, small wins cost allies, and the line between reform and destruction blurs. The narrator presents each side's arguments fairly, without preaching, and never chooses the character's methods.
